name: Cheran
overview: Cheran is a male Edomite figure identified in Scripture as the son of Dishon. His mention is brief, with no additional notes or detailed background provided beyond his tribal affiliation and lineage. As an Edomite, he is part of the descendants of Esau, which situates him within the broader biblical history of Israel's neighboring peoples.
namesAndTitles: The name Cheran appears once in the biblical record without a provided meaning or divine origin. It is simply a proper name recorded in Genesis 36:26, offering no further insight into its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Cheran as the son of Dishon, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family connections or relationships are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Cheran's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the Edomite lineage. His mention serves to document the descendants of Esau, contributing to the biblical record of nations and peoples related to Israel. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the thoroughness of Scripture in preserving the heritage of God's creation.
